transcript.text:
Thank you all for flagging these issues. Let me summarize what I'm hearing before I propose a sequence:

1. Jon — Thermocouple recalibration needed before the production window, 2 hours. This must be completed before any batch runs.
2. Priya — Batch Q requires 15 first-piece hardness tests completed and held for review before release. This impacts Q's timing.
3. Carlos — Batch R's alloy charge will oxidize if staged at the furnace bay for more than 4 hours, so R must run first.
4. Elena — Gas analyzer failed bump test; spare must be installed before any batch runs.

So we have two pre-run requirements (thermocouple recalibration and gas analyzer replacement) that must be completed before any batch starts, and R must be first in the sequence due to the oxidation constraint.

Given all of this, my proposed sequence is: R first, then Q, then P. R must lead due to the material oxidation limit. Q second, with the 15 first-piece hardness tests built into its timing. P last.

Before I finalize and release the schedule, I need sign-off from each of you. Can maintenance, quality, logistics, and process safety confirm they approve this sequence and that the pre-run tasks (recalibration and gas analyzer replacement) will be completed before startup?
